rules.statement: When loading private key material from a file, read it into a sensitive buffer and decode it into a sensitive character buffer that goes straight to the secret-key factory, never into an ordinary string or array.
rules.why: How keys are loaded decides where the private key's bytes live in the process; ordinary strings and arrays leave copies that can't be cleared.
rules.check: Look for key-loading code that uses File.ReadAllText/ReadAllBytes, string or byte[] locals, or Encoding.GetString for PEM or other private key content instead of sensitive buffer types.

rules.statement: Don't accept a private key's text as a configuration value; load private keys from files (such as mounted PEM secrets) or a key provider that configuration only names.
rules.why: A private key in a configuration value ends up in logs and in dumps of the configuration.
rules.check: Look for options properties or configuration keys that hold PEM text, base64 key bytes or JWK private parameters directly.

rules.statement: Check that a configured name refers to a registered resource (key ring, provider, keyed service) at startup and on every configuration change, not first at the request that uses it.
rules.why: A misspelled name that fails only on first use stays hidden until a user signs in, long after the host started or the configuration changed.
rules.check: Look for configuration that names a keyed service or named resource where nothing validates the name exists until a request resolves it.

rules.statement: Check whether a named resource exists through the abstraction that resolves it (for example a provider's Has… method), not by querying keyed dependency injection or the underlying store directly.
rules.why: A host can replace the provider with a source that isn't keyed DI, and a check that bypasses it would refuse names that the replacement source finds.
rules.check: Look for validation code that calls IServiceProviderIsKeyedService or GetKeyedService directly when a provider interface is the seam that resolves the resource.

rules.statement: Make an existence check that runs on every configuration change answer without loading the resource, for example without reading key files or decoding keys.
rules.why: Loading in the check reads every file on every change, and a load failure would refuse the configuration for a reason the name doesn't show.
rules.check: Look for configuration-change validators that call GetKeyRing, load keys or read files just to find out whether a name exists.

rules.statement: When a key file fails to parse, throw an exception whose message names both the logical owner (such as the key ring) and the file path.
rules.why: The operator has to know which configured entry and which file are wrong to fix a failed key load.
rules.check: Look for key-loading failures that throw or rethrow without the ring or entry name and the path in the message.

rules.statement: Have an options validator report one failure message per problem found, such as a missing name, an empty entry, a missing file or a duplicate id, rather than stopping at the first one.
rules.why: Startup validation should show every configuration problem at once.
rules.check: Look for IValidateOptions implementations that return on the first failure or merge several problems into one generic message.

rules.statement: Resolve a relative file path from configuration against the host's content root, and use an absolute path as given.
rules.why: Relative paths otherwise depend on the process's current directory.
rules.check: Look for configured file paths passed to file APIs without combining relative paths with IHostEnvironment.ContentRootPath.
